page: Microsoft Azure D128as_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Configured with 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores at up to 4.5 GHz, the instance delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 512.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core). It contains no local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs, relying on remote premium storage capabilities and CPU instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES for computational workloads.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance in the top tier (top 10%) across multiple intensive compute and throughput metrics. The system achieves a multi-core stress-ng rating of 232,585.66 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 28,721.0, accompanied by a PassMark CPU score of 134,134.92. Memory bandwidth reaches 386.84 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 189.84 GB/sec for large writes. Application benchmarks demonstrate strong scale, producing 178.44 million Redis SET operations per second and 109.94 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

In qualitative terms, the D128as_v7 provides strong resource density for organizations requiring significant parallel core counts alongside large memory pools. Architectural tradeoffs involve the lack of bundled local NVMe storage, meaning disk-bound operations rely strictly on network storage attachments, and the absence of discrete accelerators, which limits large-scale model inference despite respectable CPU-driven AVX-512 performance.

The instance is well suited for large relational databases, extensive in-memory caching tiers, large-scale software compilation, distributed web server fleets, and enterprise CI/CD orchestration workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D128as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It provides 128 dedicated vCPUs (64 physical cores) and 512.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, the instance features AVX-512 vector support but includes no local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing places the server in the top tier for multi-core performance, achieving a multi-core stress-ng score of 232,585.66, 178.44 million Redis SET operations per second, and 109.94 GB/sec in web serving throughput. Read memory bandwidth achieves 386.84 GB/sec on uncached blocks. Without attached local ephemeral disks, it relies on network storage, making it suited for enterprise database clusters, parallel software compilation, and large-scale in-memory data processing.
